_what: What the money guard on public.organizations ACTUALLY DOES, measured by running it - not by reading its source.
_why_this_replaced_parsing_the_sql: Three versions of this check parsed the migration text with regexes, and all three reported green while every money column was unlocked. A comment in front of a clause, a nested IF, the words RAISE EXCEPTION inside a string, a later migration that merely QUOTED the function, a DISABLE TRIGGER - each one fooled a parser, and each fix grew a new hole. Text cannot answer 'is this column protected'. Running the guard can: the database is the only thing that cannot lie about its own behaviour, and a disabled trigger refuses nothing, which a probe sees and a parser never will.
_how_it_was_measured: For every column on organizations, twice: (A) as a plain org ADMIN of a QA fixture org, try to change it - 42501 means the guard REFUSED it; (B) as service_role, which the guard exempts, change it and see whether a row appears in organization_money_audit. B must be separate, because a refused write never reaches the audit trigger, so an operator probe can say nothing about whether a locked column is recorded. Every change is undone immediately and the fixture is diffed against a backup afterwards.
_regenerate_with: scripts/probe-money-guard.sql - run it against STAGING via the Supabase MCP, paste the result here, and re-run the parity query at the bottom of that file against BOTH databases.
_regenerate_when: Any migration that touches guard_organizations_locked_columns, audit_organization_money, or a trigger on organizations. The test fails and tells you to, so this is a tripwire rather than a thing to remember.
fixture_org: b177a0ea-32c6-45c9-82ac-cbb7261c2dee (Cascade Enrichment Co., a QA fixture - never a real tenant)
_full_remeasure_2026_09_30: FULL probe re-run against staging on 2026-09-30, because guard_md5 and audit_md5 both moved - which the 2026-09-29 note below said was the trigger for re-running it in full. Cause: 20260930b added stripe_pending_account_id and put it in both the guard and the audit, so the previous partial-remeasure shortcut (identical hashes prove the existing columns cannot have changed) no longer applied. The new column measured refused + audited, matching the intent lists in orgMoneyColumnsGuarded.test.ts. Nothing else moved: the column list diffed against the previous snapshot shows exactly one addition and zero removals, and unprobeable stayed empty. Fixture restored and verified clean afterwards - the row is byte-identical to the backup taken first, zero audit rows left behind, both probe tables dropped. RE-RUN AGAIN the same day for 20260930c, which puts stripe_account_id into the audit: that column measured refused + AUDITED where it had been refused and unaudited, audit_md5 moved again, and guard_md5 and columns_md5 did NOT - which is the expected signature of a change that touches the audit function and nothing else. The hashes and lists here are from that second run.
_superseded_partial_remeasure_2026_09_29: The full probe was NOT re-run. It did not need to be, and saying which parts were measured is the point. guard_md5, audit_md5 and the enabled-trigger count were read from staging on 2026-09-29 and are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the values below, so the refused/audited sets cannot have changed for any column that already existed. One column had been added since the last full probe - sub_nudges_enabled, from the sub-scheduling work, on BOTH databases - and it was measured on its own against the same QA fixture, with the same two traps (reset the JWT claim as well as the role; clean audit rows by organization_id): allowed, not audited. Correct for a feature toggle, so it joins all_columns and neither of the other two lists. The fixture was restored and verified clean afterwards: value back, zero audit rows, no probe tables left. Re-run the FULL probe the next time guard_md5 or audit_md5 moves.
_full_remeasure_2026_10_08: FULL probe re-run against staging on 2026-10-08, because 20261007c (Reschedule a session) tripped the tripwire: it says "trigger" (a pay-line guard on session_delivery_confirmations) and "organizations" (a foreign key), but touches neither the guard nor the audit. The measurement confirms it: refused, audited and unprobeable are unchanged from 2026-09-30, guard_md5 and audit_md5 unchanged. The only change is all_columns gaining review_landing_url (20261006g, a plain URL, not money). Fixture restored byte-identical, 0 leftover audit rows. Parity re-checked the same day: guard_md5, audit_md5, columns_md5 and enabled_triggers are identical on staging and prod.
_parity: PROD IS EQUIVALENT AGAIN as of 2026-09-30: 20260930b (stripe_pending_account_id plus its partial unique index and its one line in the guard and the audit) and 20260930c (stripe_account_id joins the audit) were applied to BOTH databases the same day, and guard_md5, audit_md5, columns_md5 and the enabled-trigger count were read back from prod and are byte-identical to the staging values above. Before applying, prod's live trigger bodies were diffed against what the migrations restate, so neither CREATE OR REPLACE could revert a change made on prod in the meantime - they were the pre-20260930b originals. The new trigger references were then exercised on a real prod row inside a transaction that was deliberately rolled back: the update ran, the audit trigger wrote its row, and nothing persisted. Prod carries the columns and the trigger changes ONLY; stripe-connect-onboard move mode, stripe-complete-move and /admin/platform/stripe-moves are deliberately staging-only. The CHECK constraints are equivalent too - all 21 present on both, and the one whose printed text differs (organizations_statement_descriptor_suffix_check, bracketed '(A AND B) AND C' on prod and 'A AND B AND C' on staging) was PROVEN to behave identically on 2026-09-23: the stored expression was rebuilt on a scratch table on each database and fed the same twelve values, and accept/reject matched exactly. AND is associative; the deparser just grouped them differently. No DDL was run to 'fix' it - there was nothing to fix, and re-creating a CHECK on a live prod table for a cosmetic hash match is risk for nothing. An earlier version of this note called it drift, because the parity check hashed all 21 definitions together and could not tell bracketing from a changed rule; that check now compares per constraint.
_refused: The guard REFUSED an org admin's change (42501). These are platform-admin-only.
_audited: A change to these WROTE a row to organization_money_audit.
_unprobeable: Columns the probe could not test (no legal alternative value). MUST stay empty for any money column - the test fails if one appears, because an untested column is not a protected column.
_all_columns: 69 of the table's 70 columns. `id` is excluded by the probe - it is the primary key, cannot be a money setting, and an UPDATE of it is a different kind of question. If that number ever reads as a missing column, this is why.
